newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo locks horns with postal tycoon.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo locks horns with postal tycoon.

text.p: Argentina's plans to privatise its postal service erupted in a new scandal on Friday, with two controversial men trading accusations of trying to manipulate the sale.

Postal tycoon Alfredo Yabran accused his arch-enermy, former Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo, of proposing a dubious deal to manage the mail service. "He offered me a scam," Yabran said on a television talk show.
Cavallo, who has accused Yabran of heading a "mafia" and of seeking to build a postal monopoly for criminal ends, told reporters Yabran "lied every minute."

Yabran said Cavallo, who plans to run for Congress on an "anti-crime" platform after being fired from the cabinet by President Carlos Menem, made him a proposal two years ago to participate in the mail service privatisation.

He said Cavallo offered to split the service in two with hand-picked foreign firms and also offered help to pressure other minor local players into the deal. "I was one of the few unruly ones to say no," Yabran said. "After that, the 'mobster Yabran' was born."
"That is not true," responded Cavallo, demanding a full-fledged investigation.

In the interview, Yabran denied owning or having any part in security firms that according to Cavallo have engaged in illegal activities to foster the businessman's interests. He also denied having any interest in airports, which the government also plans to privatise, and said he was planning to move out of the postal business and into tourism.

The flareup came only hours after legislators announced they will create a committee to probe the allegations of organised crime that have tainted Menem's Peronist government. The idea for the committee was born last year but given urgency by Cavallo's campaign against graft and accusations that the government was aiding Yabran.
